title: UPDATED 2026-11-04 — MVP AND MMP SCORING 4th Version (adds Reddit evidence; no score changed)
intro: The 3rd Version is unchanged. This version keeps every 3rd Version score as it was. The scores are the owner's judgment, so Claude doesn't change them. It adds what the Reddit research shows for each problem, and a note where that evidence might move a score, for the owner to decide. Three problems are added at the bottom from the Reddit sample and the market analysis short list. They're left unscored for the owner. Scoring method as before: Minimal, Valuable, Testable, Learnable.
grid: Could this move a score? (owner decides)
1. Family members hold scattered, different information about the care
Family coordination, siblings 17 (4%) / 97 (24%). Tool posts: siblings won't share the work 63, information scattered 32, updates lost in group chats 28.
Maybe Valuable: the bigger Reddit signal is siblings not helping, not only scattered information.
2. Family and doctors don't know which medicines are current
No: still a small main topic.
3. Not remembering what the doctor said and recommended
Doctors, appointments, records 10 (2%) / 88 (21%). Tool posts: doctors' offices don't share 16.
4. Access to accounts and records when the person who holds the login is unavailable
Money, insurance, legal papers 32 (8%) / 117 (28%), the second most mentioned theme. Tool posts: 132 (banks refuse 46, lost passwords 32, codes to the parent's phone 22).
Supports the High Valuable score. Testable may still be Medium.
Choosing, placing and paying for care 29 (7%) / 90 (22%).
No: still real, but not the biggest need on Reddit.
Burnout, guilt, isolation, grief 102 (25%) / 210 (51%), top again. Tool posts: doing it alone 110.
Counted inside money, insurance, legal papers 32 (8%) / 117 (28%). Tool posts: documents and POA 97.
Maybe Valuable: POA problems are concrete and common (29).
8. Knowing a parent is safe when you're not there, and trusting the alert
Safety 16 (4%) / 77 (19%). Tool posts: 59 (no way to know the parent is OK 19).
9. NEW: Dementia behavior and hard conversations (from the market analysis short list)
Care recipient refuses help 38 (9%) / 83 (20%), the second most common main topic among the named themes. Tool posts: parent forgets or refuses medications 25, won't wear the device 11.
11. NEW: Hands-on personal care, equipment and supplies
17 (4%) posts as main topic (incontinence, bedbound care, wound care, lifting, supplies).
